Town Twinning
Funding totaling €28,621 was allocated to three town twinning committees to continue their work in promoting cross-
cultural understanding and encouraging civic participation and democracy through citizen and school exchanges. The
three town twinning committees allocated funding are Waterford-St Herblain, Waterford-Ramallah and Tramore-
Cadaujac committees. Twinning relationships with Märkischer Kreis, Germany also continue to be developed between
the local authority and the municipality in Märkischer Kreis with a focus on economic and tourism opportunities.
Waterford Women’s Caucus
The Waterford Women’s Caucus, chaired by Cllr. Mary Roche, were successful in securing €10,000, following a call for
proposals under ‘Increasing Diversity and the Participation of Women in Local Government’. The funding will
contribute towards the development of an NFQ Level 8 Women in Leadership in Local Government, which is being
developed in partnership with SETU and will target female councillors from across the region; funding will also be
utilised to increase awareness of local government and opportunities for increased female participation in the build up
to the 2029 elections and increase awareness of local government amongst younger people.

The temporary steel supports for the sustainable transport
bridge are currently being removed from the river and the
pier protection system will be completed in the coming
months. 
The finishing works for the bridge are ongoing with the
installation of the edge railings, glass panels and
pedestrian barriers, thereafter the remaining finishing
works, e.g. lighting, street furniture etc. which will
commence. It is likely that the specialist final bridge
surfacing 
will 
proceed 
in 
early 
Summer 
when
temperatures and weather are more suitable.
The South Plaza will provide a landscaped public realm
area with seating, lighting, green area and bicycle
facilities. Works are well advanced; the paving is over 90%
complete, seating around the clock tower is in place and
is open to the public. Works are expected to be complete
in March 2026, at that point final snagging checks and
safety audits will be completed, in advance of the full area
being open to the public. Public access from the South
Plaza to the sustainable transport bridge will be closed off
and secured until the bridge opens to the public in 2027. 
Finishing works are continuing to the train station
building, including mechanical & electrical fitout and the
internal finishing works are well advanced. The testing &
commissioning of the various operational systems in the
station will proceed in Q2. The final rendered finish to the
northern lift shaft will be completed shortly and this
scaffolding will then be removed.

Waterford Airport
The shareholders of Waterford Regional Airport at an Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) held last
December, approved by an overwhelming majority the same investment proposal that had been agreed
by the Council in October, 2025. This approval represented a significant next step and milestone in
progressing the agreed restructuring and investment arrangements for the airport development.
It is understood that the investor has now secured Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) clearance from the
Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment (DETE). This clearance is a key regulatory requirement
and provides formal confirmation that the investor has satisfied the State’s due diligence processes and is
recognised as a bona fide entity to carry out the airport development.
The transfer of the assets of Waterford Regional Airport DAC to the investor can now proceed and is
scheduled to be finalised in March. As part of the agreed transaction structure, the investor will discharge
all existing creditor liabilities, ensuring that all outstanding debts of the company are fully settled.
The next procedural step in the process is for Waterford Regional Airport to enter into a voluntary
members’ liquidation. A further EGM of shareholders is required to formally approve this step, and it is
anticipated that this meeting will take place early next month. Subject to completion of these steps, the
developer has indicated an intention to commence works on site before the summer and the anticipated
construction programme is approximately 12 months. It is important to note that Council-owned lands
will not transfer to the investor until the agreed airport development works have been completed, in line
with the terms previously approved by the Council.

Waterford Local Enterprise Office has announced a large programme of events across 5 days during Local
Enterprise Week 2026, taking place for Waterford City and County businesses from March 2  to March 6 .
nd
th
 
This year’s Local Enterprise Week will feature many new events including informative and engaging
workshops, seminars, presentations and advice clinics aimed at local businesses, whether in pre-start,
start-up or as an established business looking to grow.
One of these new partnerships is with Buíon Phort Láirge. This collaboration delivers a practical workshop
designed to help you refine your sales approach and strengthen your business pitch. The session will
focus on real-world techniques that help you communicate your value more clearly, connect more
effectively with potential customers, and turn conversations into opportunities.
 
The Lunchtime Bites series heads to three county Enterprise Centres throughout the week. These sessions
are a great opportunity to visit your local Enterprise Centre, learn about the facilities and supports
available, and see how the centre could support your business now or in the future. 
The Local Enterprise Office also celebrates International Women’s Day with Waterford Chamber,
Dungarvan Chamber and Network Waterford supporting events across the week.
Waterford Local Enterprise Office is delighted to work in conjunction with various key business support
organisations and state agencies, including Enterprise Ireland, Network Waterford, Buíon Phort Láirge,
Dungarvan & West Waterford Chamber and Waterford Chamber, to provide a programme that gives
entrepreneurs and businesses opportunities to help them on the path to growth.

NPF 2025 Implementation: Housing Growth Requirements
Further to the planning report in February, a copy of the Chief Executive Report on Development Plan Core
Strategy Annual Monitoring & NPF Implementation: Housing Growth Requirements has now been
circulated to Council. This report concludes that the development plan, as varied, has zoned a sufficient
quantum of land to meet the housing growth requirements for Waterford City and County during the
lifetime of the development plan (July 2028). The report also concluded that notwithstanding variation
no.1 of the plan, greater certainty in the development plan would support the release of appropriately
located and serviced/serviceable residentially zoned land, and improve housing delivery in the longer term
and as such, further consideration of these issues will be required, having regard to the broader strategic
policy objectives and aims of the development plan. 
Further to this conclusion, Waterford City & County Council will soon commence a process to seek
expressions of interest from landowners/developers with regard to the timing and release of sequentially
located land for residential development, in order to streamline and phasing the delivery of essential
enabling service infrastructure by the council, service providers, and the private sector. 
Ultimately, while this process may result in the rezoning of land for residential use, given the quantum and
spatial context of land zoned for R1 and SRR in the development plan, it is unlikely that this process will
support new zoning of land for residential purposes beyond the spatial extent of current R1/SRR lands, as
such land would potentially be outside built footprints of settlements and outside defined CSO settlement
boundaries. The principal objective of the process will be to support development of land which can be
demonstrated to be sequential, compact and infrastructure-led, and more importantly consistent with the
development plan outcomes and the policy objectives of chapter 2 Spatial Vision & Core Strategy and
chapter 7 Housing & Sustainable Communities. The process will be used however to finetune the
phasing/tiering of land for residential development, the sequencing of infrastructure delivery and the
potential rezoning of land from an existing land use to new residential land use. 
Along with the emerging details from this process, it is intended to commence a new variation (no. 2) of
the development plan in late Q2/ early Q3. 
We will workshop relevant details of the potential development plan variation in the coming months with
the plenary council and SPC.

Community Monuments Fund
Six applications were submitted to the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage under the 2026
Community Monuments Fund. Stream 1 offers grants of up to €100,000 aimed at essential repairs and capital
works for the conservation of archaeological monuments. Stream 2 offers grants up to €30,000 for
development of Conservation Management Plans/Reports/Assessments and detailed Specification of Works that
are aimed at identifying measures for conservation and maintenance of archaeological monuments. The
outcome will be known in early April.
Cultural Commemorations Fund
Waterford City and County Council have submitted a cultural commemorations programme to the Department
of Culture, Communications and Sport for allocation of funding. Events planned for 2026 include
commemorating the bicentenary of the 1826 Parliamentary Elections which paved the way for Catholic
Emancipation and the 400  anniversary of the 1626 Great Governing Charter which empowered the Mayor of
Waterford City to hold admiralty courts within the harbour and underlies the annual tradition of claiming the
waters in Waterford Estuary.

ACTIVE LAND MANAGEMENT AND DERELICT SITES TEAM
The team is currently addressing 377 properties, classified as either derelict or potentially derelict. In recent weeks
and months, there has been a significant increase in activity, with 146 properties now listed on the Derelict Sites
Register. Engaging with property owners or their representatives is essential for addressing dereliction issues and
understanding the numerous factors that contribute to the properties' current condition. 
The level of activity in the property market concerning vacant and derelict properties has notably increased. Among
the properties we have identified as derelict, several have been reintroduced to the private market voluntarily, with
some currently at the 'sale agreed' or 'to let' stages. We are actively engaging with the new owners of these
properties to ensure they are fully informed of their obligations under the Derelict Sites Act 1990. We are also seeing
a consistent number of planning applications for property refurbishment/ extension, and the level of work ongoing
on individual properties is clear from driving around the city and county. 
We are advising property owners of the vacant property refurbishment grant if the property is suitable for residential
use. This grant has contributed to a significant rise in the number of derelict and vacant properties currently
available on the market.
With time and effort, through collaboration with owners, financial institutions, and other departments, there are
definite options for the positive redevelopment and revitalisation of many derelict sites.

Housing Infrastructure Investment Fund (HIIF) Applications 
The Government recently launched the Housing Infrastructure Investment Fund (HIIF), a €1 billion initiative
designed to activate and accelerate housing delivery nationally, over a five year period. 
The HIIF is managed by the Housing Activation Office and the first call for applications closed at the end of
February. Under the terms of this initial call, only the Land Development Agency (LDA) and local authorities were
eligible to apply, and projects under this initial call must have full planning permission in place and be “shovel
ready”. A total of three applications have been submitted in respect of Waterford, namely one by the LDA and two
by Waterford City and County Council (WCCC).
The LDA application relates to public infrastructure required to facilitate residential development at the North
Quays. The LDA have been working with Harcourt Developments, trading as Hopcast Limited, on the residential
elements of their commercial project, since they were granted planning permission in May of last year. In addition,
WCCC submitted two further applications under the HIIF: one in respect of a new road required to open up
residential lands for development at Carrickpherish, and the other in relation to necessary storm water drainage
infrastructure required to facilitate housing development in Dungarvan. Both of these projects have Part 8 planning
approval in place. It is understood that the Housing Activation Office will have a relatively quick turnaround on
decisions on the first call for applications under the HIIF.

RMCEI Reporting Update
During this reporting period, the team has focused on the development of the 2026 inspection plan and the preparation
of the annual inspection activity report in line with the requirements of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) under
the RMCEI (Recommendation on Minimum Criteria for Environmental Inspections) framework.
The RMCEI plan sets out the Council’s proposed environmental inspection and enforcement programme for 2026. It
outlines the priority sectors, risk-based inspection approach, resource allocation, and compliance monitoring activities
to be undertaken throughout the year. The plan ensures that inspections are carried out in a structured, consistent, and
proportionate manner, targeting higher-risk activities while maintaining appropriate oversight across all regulated sites.

Storm Chandra
Following the Storm Chandra weather event, the Council’s Severe Weather Assessment Team met to conduct a post
event review, as is standard practice after significant weather events. It should be noted that the storm caused
significant damage to the road network, with a total of 37 different locations been identified where significant
pavement damage occurred . While remedial works have been undertaken, these repairs represent temporary
measures only, pending the implementation of permanent restoration works and/or climate resilient drainage
improvements works. The estimated cost for these reinstatement works is in excess of €8m and a funding application
has been submitted to the Department of Transport requesting an additional €8m allocation under the severe
weather category.  The Council are also proposing a number of measures to strengthen preparedness and resilience
going forward and same will be included in our updated Severe Weather Plan, which will be incorporated in our
Major Emergency Plan. A key priority will be the identification and mapping of locations most at risk of flooding
during severe weather events, to ensure that preparedness measures are targeted. We will also continue to work
closely with local communities, in particular the recently selected community hubs, to ensure that most vulnerable
residents are supported during weather events. We will also strengthen liaison with Uisce Éireann to ensure
responsibilities and enhanced information sharing during incidents, where water and wastewater infrastructure is
impacted. The role of the Fire Service during severe weather events will be reviewed to ensure that its deployment
remains aligned with its primary emergency response responsibilities. We will also reengage with OPW for: funding
support towards flood relief schemes previously put forward in flood risk areas that have so far been unsuccessful;
and for funding support towards interim measures (e.g. flood protection barriers) that can be put in place, pending
support for full flood relief schemes. The Chief Executive and Director of Services attended a meeting recently with
Minister Boxer Moran and senior officials in the OPW to present Waterford’s case for funding support.
